title: First Seizure in Adults: Assessment and Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult first suspected seizure: immediate reversible causes, mimic assessment, investigation and urgent specialist referral using NICE NG217.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi first-seizure guideline was opened.
Driving restrictions require current Saudi legal guidance.
SFDA status is not applicable because routine antiseizure treatment is not initiated here.

pathophysiology.summary: Transient hypersynchronous cortical activity can produce motor, sensory, autonomic or awareness changes. Metabolic disturbance, infection, toxin or structural brain disease may provoke an acute symptomatic seizure. Syncope and cardiac arrhythmia can mimic epileptic seizure. Recurrence risk depends on cause, examination, EEG and imaging findings.
keyMechanisms: Transient hypersynchronous cortical activity can produce motor, sensory, autonomic or awareness changes.
Metabolic disturbance, infection, toxin or structural brain disease may provoke an acute symptomatic seizure.
Syncope and cardiac arrhythmia can mimic epileptic seizure.
Recurrence risk depends on cause, examination, EEG and imaging findings.

references.title: NICE NG217: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

symptoms: Witnessed tonic-clonic movement, focal symptoms, altered awareness, tongue injury, incontinence or post-event confusion.
physicalSigns: Postictal confusion, focal neurological deficit, injury or abnormal vital signs; examination may normalise.
redFlags: Ongoing seizure, repeated seizure without recovery, persistent focal deficit, meningism, severe headache, pregnancy, major injury, hypoglycaemia or cardiorespiratory instability.
precipitants: Sleep deprivation, alcohol or substance use/withdrawal, metabolic disturbance, infection, stroke, tumour and interacting medicines.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Prodrome, posture and rapid recovery may suggest circulatory cause; obtain a 12-lead ECG.
Diagnosis requires expert assessment and should not be inferred from one atypical feature.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Features before, during and after the event
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use eyewitness account and available video alongside examination.

references.title: NICE NG217: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Identify cardiac conditions that can mimic seizure and escalate accordingly.
ruleIn.normalValue: Sinus rhythm without acute conduction or ischaemic abnormality

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Order as part of ED first-seizure assessment and interpret against the clinical presentation.

ruleOut.testName: Capillary glucose and directed metabolic tests

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Correct immediately and investigate the cause.

ruleOut.normalValue: No epileptiform activity; this does not exclude epilepsy

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise and identify emergencies
actions: Treat ongoing seizure, hypoglycaemia, injury, infection or cardiorespiratory instability through the relevant emergency pathway.
Document witness history, postictal state, neurological examination and medicines/substances.

clinicalManagement.title: Check mimics and causes
actions: Obtain 12-lead ECG and capillary glucose; add laboratory and imaging tests based on clinical suspicion.
Do not use EEG to exclude epilepsy.

clinicalManagement.title: Urgent specialist referral and safety advice
actions: Refer to a clinician with expertise in first seizures and epilepsy.
Advise against driving pending current Saudi specialist/legal guidance and discuss bathing, heights, machinery and supervision risks.

medicationPlan.note: Do not initiate routine long-term antiseizure medicine solely from this pathway; treatment depends on expert diagnosis, recurrence risk and cause.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Appointment within 2 weeks after a first suspected seizure.

teaching.scope: Adult first suspected seizure: immediate reversible causes, mimic assessment, investigation and urgent specialist referral using NICE NG217.
pitfalls: Starting long-term treatment before cause and recurrence risk are assessed, unless an emergency specialist indication exists.
keyPoints: A normal EEG does not exclude epilepsy.

references.title: NICE NG217: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

patientEducation: Give written seizure first-aid and safety advice to the patient and family.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid sleep deprivation, alcohol binges, unsupervised swimming, heights and hazardous machinery until specialist advice.
mdtReferrals: First-seizure/neurology clinic, cardiology if ECG abnormal, and emergency specialties for identified causes.
dischargeCriteria: Returned to baseline, no acute red flag, responsible supervision and urgent referral plus written safety advice arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Ensure first-seizure assessment within 2 weeks; if EEG is requested, target completion within 72 hours of the event.
